day_shape: 76 items: overnight US-Saudi joint strikes on Hashd al-Shaabi bases in Iraq dominate regime and Israeli coverage, State Dept designates two IRGC-linked Hormuz insurance entities, Hezbollah drone hits IDF bulldozer in south Lebanon, Reuters reports 400 Chinese MANPADS bound for Iran.

threads.label: US-Saudi strikes on Iraqi militias
threads.summary: Iraq's National Security Council under PM Ali al-Zaidi held an emergency meeting condemning overnight joint US-Saudi strikes on Hashd al-Shaabi bases across several provinces. Defa Press claimed 10 fighters killed and posted funeral footage; Al-Nujaba demanded expulsion of US forces, while the Jerusalem Post framed the strikes as a milestone in US-Saudi ties.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz sanctions and diplomacy
threads.summary: The State Department designated the Persian Gulf Marine Insurance Company and Hormuz Safe Marine Services Authority, two IRGC-backed entities running coercive insurance schemes in the Strait. FM Araghchi discussed Hormuz with EU's Kaja Kallas; former UAE diplomat Obaid al-Zaabi said the UAE will not accept Iranian control or tolls; a Ghalibaf-linked paper asked whether China defused Iran's oil weapon.

threads.label: South Lebanon: Hezbollah drone strike, IDF operations
threads.summary: The IDF confirmed an unmanned engineering vehicle was hit overnight by a Hezbollah explosive drone at Ali Taher Ridge — the first such attack since the late-June framework agreement — and said Israel will respond. Israeli troops also demolished a 55-metre Hezbollah tunnel command centre near a UNIFIL building in Haddatha; Defa Press described the incident as Israeli 'aggression' with incendiary bullets.

threads.label: Iran nuclear and arms procurement
threads.summary: A senior Israeli official told the Jerusalem Post that Iran is keeping centrifuges at Pickaxe Mountain and that Israel judges the nuclear programme set back but not destroyed, warning of further action. Reuters and Iran International reported Iran is set to receive within weeks up to 400 Chinese shoulder-fired air-defence launchers under a $60-70 million deal.

threads.label: Iran espionage and internal security
threads.summary: Israeli authorities indicted an IDF reservist from a classified unit for contact with a foreign agent and attempted delivery of information to Iran, charged at Tel Aviv District Court on July 16. Iran's Ministry of Intelligence announced the dismantling of four takfiri cells and arrest of 15 suspects in Sistan and Baluchestan; Iran International reported a teenage girl shot dead during January Tehran protests.

threads.label: Ukraine-Iran Caspian incident fallout
threads.summary: Iranian and Western officials told the New York Times that Tehran considered striking a Ukrainian Black Sea port in response to a Ukrainian attack on an Iranian ship in the Caspian, but opted against it after diplomacy. Iran International framed the Ukrainian strike as messaging rather than a new front.

threads.label: Regime messaging: vengeance and Arbaeen
threads.summary: Khamenei's office posted that 'every martyr is a file for vengeance' and pledged no restraint in avenging children's blood. IRIB and Defa Press ran heavy Arbaeen coverage, reporting over 2 million pilgrims exiting land borders and 625,000 vehicles moving to the Iraqi frontier.

events.title: The Israeli army says it demolished an underground Hezbollah command center, built beneath a construction material factory in southern Lebanon. During operations in the village of Haddatha, inside the IDF's south Lebanon buffer zone, troops uncovered a 55-meter-long tunnel, the military says. The IDF says the tunnel featured three rooms, and it was used by Hezbollah as a command center. It was built beneath a construction material factory and located some 300 meters from a UNIFIL building, according to the army. Nearby, troops also located a pit with dozens of weapons in it, the IDF adds. Combat engineers blew up the tunnel this week.
